subject: Completion assurance for nightly async batches — proposed SLA amendment
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>

Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Completion assurance for nightly batches

Hi Connor,

Quick follow-up from our SRE sync — our ingestion pipeline runs nightly bulk inference jobs (~3M records) and our compliance team needs clearer guarantees for job finalization and dedupe semantics. Two specific asks: 1) an explicit completion window (how long you guarantee a job will either succeed or land in a failed state), and 2) confirmation on idempotency/retry semantics so we don't process duplicates when we auto-retry from our side.

We don't need hard credits yet, but would like a short SLA amendment that spells out: completion window, safe-retry guidance (max retries, backoff), an idempotency token model (what keys we should send), and observability hooks (webhook or status endpoint we can poll). Can you share a proposal we can show procurement?

Best,
Tom
Director of Platform
Acme Analytics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.inference>

Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Completion assurance for nightly batches

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a short SLA amendment draft and a one-page diagram of the proposed completion assurance flow. High level proposal below; attached doc has contractual language for procurement/legal.

Summary proposal (quick bullets):
- Completion window: nightly bulk jobs (batch <10M records) — finalization within 24 hours from job start 95% of the time; 99% within 36 hours. Jobs still in-flight at 36h are marked "long-tail" and will be visible on the status endpoint and eligible for the remediation playbook.
- Idempotency model: supply a deterministic idempotency_token per job (customer-generated UUID). For per-record dedupe we recommend an item_id per-row; Redwood will honor at-most-once semantics within a 72h dedupe window for identical item_id + job id combinations.
- Retry policy: Redwood will perform server-side safe-retries for transient infra failures (up to 3 internal attempts with exponential backoff starting at 30s). Customer-initiated retries should include same idempotency_token to avoid duplicates.
- Finalization checkpoint: Redwood emits a finalization event (webhook + status endpoint) when a job transitions to Succeeded/Failed/Long-tail. Heartbeat pings every 10 minutes while active; absent heartbeats trigger alerting.
- Remediation & credits: for missed 95% target (monthly), proposal includes crediting a pro-rated portion of that month's API usage (detailed in attached amend). For exceptions (scheduled maintenance), we'll provide a 7-day advance notice window when possible.

Next steps: Marissa and Ben — can you review the attached language (ACME_SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf) for legal/pricing signals? Tom/Sarah — if that looks directionally right, I'll circulate a concise amendment for signatures.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>

Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 18:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Completion assurance for nightly batches

Connor — quick comments from pricing/legal ops:
- The 95% / 99% band is okay but suggest we tighten the remediation wording: instead of an open "pro-rated credit", we should propose a tiered credit matrix (e.g., 2.5% for month if monthly aggregate <95%, 5% if <90%) — attach a redlined table in the PDF.
- Dedupe window: 72h is acceptable but call out storage/retention impact (we keep dedupe metadata for 14 days for customers on Dedicated). Public hosted customers should default to 7 days unless they purchase the extended retention add-on.
- Retry description: clarify that server-side retries are idempotent only if the customer provides item_id per-row; otherwise we can only guarantee best-effort and will recommend client-side dedupe.

I'll inline a suggested paragraph for the amendment and replace the generic credit language. Ben — can you sanity-check cost exposure for stored dedupe metadata?

-Marissa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick cost note: retaining dedupe metadata for 14 days for a 3M-record/night workload at typical item_id sizes would increase storage by roughly 1.2TB/month (index + metadata). If Acme wants 14 days we should attach an add-on line item; 7 days still covers most dup scenarios and keeps exposure low. The tiered credit matrix looks fine — recommend we cap cumulative monthly credits at 10% to limit financial risk.

Connor — I updated the PDF with the credit table and the retention options. See attached. Once Tom confirms the terms, we can route to legal/finance and send for signature.

-Ben

Connor / Marissa / Ben — thanks, this is helpful and directionally acceptable. Two small asks before we move to signature: 1) can the dedupe window for hosted customers be 10 days (not 7)? That gives our ops team extra buffer. 2) for the webhook finalization event — can you include a job-level "finalization_reason" field (Succeeded|Failed|Long-tail|Cancelled) and a list of failed item_ids (truncated to 1K entries) when applicable?

If you can confirm those two items (and reflect the 10-day hosted retention in the amendment), we'll sign. Happy to do DocuSign once updated.

Best,
Tom
